writing.sample_en:
【参考范文 · 166 词】写作无唯一标准答案，以下为达标示范
With the increasing application of AI technology, there is a growing concern that it may negatively impact human creativity. In my view, this worry is well-grounded, for excessive reliance on AI can gradually dull our capacity to think and create independently.
The reason is straightforward. Creativity is a muscle that strengthens only through active practice. When we ask AI to generate essays, ideas, or solutions at the click of a button, we skip the very struggle that sparks original thinking. Take my own experience as an example. Last semester, I turned to an AI tool whenever an assignment felt difficult. Although the drafts came quickly, I soon realized that my mind had grown lazy: I could no longer brainstorm freely, and my writing lost its personal voice.
Therefore, the concern deserves our serious attention. AI should serve as a helpful assistant rather than a replacement for our own minds. Only by keeping our thinking active can we ensure that technology enriches, rather than erodes, human creativity.

cloze.title: 2025年6月·第3套 英语六级完形填空（选词填空） · 26–35 题答案与解析

passages.en: The slow progress of women in elective office is frustrating for some political observers and experts—including myself. Achieving gender equality in Congress is an important goal. This is because the number of women involved in legislative decisions has significant __(26)__ for all the policies that governments __(27)__ . Female legislators are more likely than men to introduce, speak about and work to pass policies that disproportionately affect women and girls, such as paid family leave, pay __(28)__ and gender-based violence.
passages.zh: 女性在民选公职中的缓慢进展令一些政治观察家和专家感到沮丧，其中也包括我自己。在国会实现性别平等是一个重要目标。这是因为参与立法决策的女性人数会对政府制定的所有政策产生重大影响。与男性立法者相比，女性立法者更有可能提出、谈论并推动通过那些对女性和女孩产生不成比例影响的政策，例如带薪家庭假、同工同酬以及基于性别的暴力问题相关政策。

passages.en: Having more women in Congress also fosters a greater sense of connection between female voters and government. In addition, it __(29)__ women's sense that government cares about their concerns and inspires young women to become more politically engaged.
passages.zh: 国会中有更多女性也会增进女性选民与政府之间的联系感。此外，这会增强女性对于政府关心她们所关注问题的感受，并激励年轻女性更加积极地参与政治。

passages.en: While women are underrepresented in governments around the globe, it is a particularly __(30)__ problem in the United States. Currently, the U.S. ranks 73rd in the world when it comes to female representation in government.
passages.zh: 尽管女性在世界各国政府中的代表性都不足，但这一问题在美国尤其严峻。目前，就女性在政府中的代表性而言，美国在世界排名第73位。

passages.en: But the reason women are so __(31)__ underrepresented in U.S. government is not because they face resistance from voters or struggle to raise money. On the contrary, decades of research shows that female candidates raise as much money and win as often as male politicians with similar __(32)__ .
passages.zh: 但是，女性在美国政府中严重代表不足，并不是因为她们受到选民的抵制或难以筹集资金。恰恰相反，数十年的研究表明，拥有相似资历的女性候选人与男性政治人物筹集的资金一样多，获胜的频率也一样高。

passages.en: Rather, the slow progress of women in politics is a tale of two political parties.
passages.zh: 相反，女性在政治领域进展缓慢，实际上是两个政党的故事。

passages.en: In the next Congress, there will be 107 female Democratic lawmakers and 42 female Republican lawmakers in the Senate and House combined.
passages.zh: 在下一届国会中，参议院和众议院合计将有107名女性民主党议员和42名女性共和党议员。

passages.en: In order for women to gain half of the seats in Congress, more women need to run, __(33)__ on Republican tickets. This will require the Republican Party as a whole to __(34)__ recruiting women—and not just for one election cycle, but in a __(35)__ way.
passages.zh: 为了让女性获得国会一半的席位，需要有更多女性参选，尤其是作为共和党候选人参选。这将要求共和党全党把招募女性置于优先地位，而且不能只持续一个选举周期，而要以一种持久的方式进行。

wordbank.gloss: 增强、支持（第三人称单数）
持续的；维持（过去式/过去分词）

rows.text: B) consequences名词
形容词 significant + ___ + for 介词短语
have consequences for 是高频固定搭配，意为'对…产生影响' 本句解释'女性议员数量对所有政策都有重要影响'，与 Female legislators are more likely than men to introduce, speak about and work to pass policies 一脉相承，consequences for policies 完全贴合。

C)credentials'资历'与 for policies 搭配不成立 credentials 指个人证书、资格，对应的是 candidate 本身，不能说'议员数量对政策有 credentials'。 F)equity义为'公平'，与 have ... for 搭不成立 have significant equity for policies 既不成搭配，也不通逻辑。 J)impetus'推动力'常用 give/provide impetus to，不用 have impetus for impetus 与 for 共现表'对…的推动'虽可，但句意偏'对政策有影响'而非'推动'，consequences 更贴。

最具迷惑性的错误词是 J) —— impetus 看似也能与 for 搭，'对…的推动'',词性也对。考生易被 has significant impetus for policies 的字面看似通顺骗到；防坑点是 have consequences for 才是英语里'对…有影响'的固定搭配，且本段紧接的例证 Female legislators are more likely than men to introduce, speak about and work to pass policies 说的是'影响政策内容'而非'推动政策出现'。
E) enact动词
定语从句 that governments + ___，缺谓语动词
enact policies 是固定搭配'颁布/制定政策' 上文谈'女性议员推动政策通过' work to pass policies that disproportionately affect women and girls，governments enact policies 与之同义，且 enact 与 policies/laws 是公认搭配。
L)prioritize'优先处理'语义偏'排序'，且要被 34 题占用 prioritize policies 也能说，但语义在'优先排序'而非'制定'；而且 34 题需要 prioritize 与 recruiting 搭配，词只能用一次。
F) equity名词
并列名词项 paid family leave, pay ___ and gender-based violence
pay equity = 同工同酬，影响女性的典型议题 本段例证 policies that disproportionately affect women and girls 列举与女性相关的政策议题，pay equity（同工同酬）与 paid family leave、gender-based violence 同属'女性权益'范畴，是英语世界讨论性别平等的高频术语。
J)impetuspay impetus 不成搭配，且与女性议题无关 impetus 是'推动力'，不与 pay 构成复合名词，也无法作为'议题'与 paid family leave 并列。
A) bolsters动词
主语 it + ___ + 宾语 women's sense
bolster one's sense 是'增强某人的…感'的常见搭配 上文 Having more women in Congress also fosters a greater sense of connection 已用 foster；本句用并列动词继续推进同向语义，bolsters women's sense that government cares 自然衔接。
M)sufficessuffices 是不及物动词，不能带宾语 suffice 表'足够'，常说 it suffices to do/that...，后面跟从句或不定式；不能直接接 women's sense 作宾语，语法不通。
I) formidable形容词
不定冠词 a + 副词 particularly + ___ + 名词 problem
与 problem 构成常见搭配'棘手的问题' 上下文交代美国排名第 73 the U.S. ranks 73rd in the world，说明这一问题在美国'尤其棘手'；formidable problem 是英语高频搭配，与 particularly 程度副词自然衔接。
K)lavish词义指向'奢华、铺张'，与 problem 不搭 lavish 多形容花费、款待，无法描述社会问题的严重程度。 O)tenured义为'终身聘任的'，专用于职位 tenured 常见搭配是 tenured professor/position，修饰 problem 完全不通。
D) dramatically副词
be 动词 are + ___ + 过去分词 underrepresented
强调'代表性偏低'的程度，呼应美国排第 73 上文已用 particularly formidable 渲染问题严重，本句继续追问'为何如此严重地代表不足'；dramatically underrepresented 是英文报道里固定的'程度极大'表达。

G)especially意为'尤其'，常引出比较或例子 especially 通常需要一个比较对象或后接具体范畴（especially on Republican tickets 那种），单独修饰 underrepresented 表程度则不自然，且 G 已被 33 题强需占用。 H)evasively义为'回避地、含糊地'，与 underrepresented 逻辑不通 evasively 多修饰 answer/respond 等言语动词，描述'代表性不足'毫无语义关联。
C) credentials名词
介词 with + 形容词 similar + ___

candidates with similar credentials = '资历相当的候选人' 本段反驳一种误解 not because they face resistance from voters or struggle to raise money，再以研究为据 female candidates raise as much money and win as often as male politicians with similar __(32)__. 进行同等条件下的对比，credentials（资历）正是这种'公平比较'的基准。
J)impetus'推动力'不可用 similar 衡量，且与候选人能力比较无关 similar impetus 在政客比较语境下毫无意义，无法构成对照基准。
G) especially副词
逗号后 + ___ + 介词短语 on Republican tickets

聚焦到共和党票上，呼应'两党之别'主旨 上文 there will be 107 female Democratic lawmakers and 42 female Republican lawmakers 表明共和党女议员人数远少；本句强调 more women need to run, especially on Republican tickets，正是把'更多女性参选'的火力点向共和党聚焦。
H)evasively义不搭 evasively 描述'回避地、含糊地'参选毫无意义，逻辑指向反。
L) prioritize动词
情态动词 to + ___ + 动名词 recruiting
prioritize doing 是'优先去做某事'的固定搭配 上文已点出共和党女议员稀少 42 female Republican lawmakers，本句号召共和党把'招募女性'放到优先级首位，prioritize recruiting women 既合搭配也合语义。
N) sustained形容词
介词 in + 限定词 a + ___ + 名词 way
与 not just for one election cycle 形成时间维度的对照——'持续的' 本句要点 not just for one election cycle, but in a __(35)__ way：not just one cycle 暗含'不止一次性'，与之对照的正是'持续地、长期地'，in a sustained way 是英文里强调长期坚持的固定写法。
K)lavish义为'奢华的'，与时间维度无关 in a lavish way 形容方式'铺张奢侈'，与'不止一次选举周期'的对照无任何逻辑联系。
最具迷惑性的错误词是 K) —— lavish 与 way 搭配看似通顺。in a lavish way 字面读起来似乎成立，考生不细看上下文易误选；防坑点是利用 not just A, but B 的对照结构——A 是 one election cycle（短期），B 必为'长期持续'，sustained 才合方向。

longreading.title: 2025年6月·第3套 英语六级长篇阅读（信息匹配） 第 1 篇 · 36–45 题答案与解析

passages.en: A) I can be a reluctant socialiser. I'm sometimes secretly pleased when social plans are called off. I get restless a few hours into a hangout. I even once went on a free 10-day silent meditation(冥想) retreat—not for the meditation, but for the silence.
passages.zh: 我有时不太情愿参加社交活动。有时社交计划被取消，我还会暗自高兴。聚会几小时后，我就会坐立不安。我甚至曾经参加过一次免费的十天静默冥想营——并不是为了冥想，而是为了享受寂静。

passages.en: B) So I can relate to author Anneli Rufus, who wrote in *Party of One: The Loners' Manifesto*: "When parents on TV shows punished their kids by ordering them to go to their rooms, I was confused. I loved my room. Being there behind a locked door was a treat. To me a punishment was being ordered to play games with my cousin Louis."
passages.zh: 所以我能理解作家 Anneli Rufus。她在《独自一人：孤独者宣言》中写道：“电视节目里，父母惩罚孩子时常常会命令他们回自己的房间，我对此感到困惑。我喜欢自己的房间。待在上锁的房间里对我来说是一种享受。对我而言，惩罚是被命令去和我的表弟 Louis 玩游戏。”

passages.en: C) Unsocial tendencies like these are often far from ideal. Abundant research shows the harms of social isolation, considered a serious public health problem in countries that have rapidly ageing populations (though talk of a 'loneliness epidemic' may be exaggerated). In the UK, the Royal College of General Practitioners says that loneliness has the same risk level for premature death as diabetes. Strong social connections are important for cognitive functioning, motor function and a smoothly running immune system.
passages.zh: 像这样的不合群倾向往往并不理想。大量研究表明，社会隔离会造成危害；在那些人口迅速老龄化的国家，社会隔离被视为一个严重的公共卫生问题（不过，“孤独流行病”的说法可能被夸大了）。在英国，皇家全科医师学会表示，孤独导致过早死亡的风险程度与糖尿病相同。牢固的社会联系对于认知功能、运动功能以及免疫系统顺畅运转都十分重要。

passages.en: D) This is especially clear from cases of extreme social isolation. Examples of people kept in captivity, children kept isolated in abusive orphanages, and prisoners kept in solitary confinement all show how prolonged solitude can lead to hallucinations(幻觉) and other forms of mental instability.
passages.zh: 极端社会隔离的案例尤其清楚地说明了这一点。被囚禁的人、被隔离在受虐待的孤儿院中的儿童，以及被单独监禁的囚犯，这些例子都表明，长期独处可能导致幻觉和其他形式的精神不稳定。

passages.en: E) But these are severe and involuntary cases of aloneness. For those of us who just prefer plenty of alone time, emerging research suggests some good news: there are upsides to being alone—for both our work lives and our emotional well-being.
passages.zh: 但这些都是严重且非自愿的孤独状态。对于我们这些只是喜欢拥有大量独处时间的人来说，正在出现的研究带来了一些好消息：独处有其积极的一面，既有利于我们的工作生活，也有利于我们的情绪健康。

passages.en: F) Solitude is a time for reflection, for thinking about things more deeply. In a world increasingly focused on speed and competitiveness, solitude is precious and something to be treasured. And there are benefits in learning to love your solitude.
passages.zh: 独处是一个用于反思、更加深入地思考事物的时间。在一个日益注重速度和竞争力的世界里，独处十分珍贵，值得我们珍惜。而学会享受独处也会带来益处。

passages.en: G) One key benefit of solitude is improved creativity. Gregory Feist, who focuses on the psychology of creativity at California's San Jose State University, has defined creativity as thinking or activity with two key elements: originality and usefulness. He has found that personality traits commonly associated with creativity are openness (receptiveness to new thoughts and experiences), self-confidence, and autonomy—which may include "a lack of concern for social norms" and "a preference for being alone". In fact, Feist's research on both artists and scientists shows that one of the most prominent features of creative folks is their lesser interest in socialising.
passages.zh: 独处的一个重要益处是创造力得到提升。Gregory Feist 主要研究加利福尼亚州圣何塞州立大学的创造力心理学。他将创造力定义为包含两个关键要素的思维或活动：原创性和实用性。他发现，通常与创造力相关的人格特征包括开放性（对新思想和新经历的接受程度）、自信以及自主性——自主性可能包括“不在意社会规范”和“偏好独处”。事实上，Feist 对艺术家和科学家的研究都表明，富有创造力的人最显著的特征之一，就是他们对社交活动的兴趣较低。

passages.en: H) One reason for this is that such people are likely to spend sustained time alone working on their craft. Plus, Feist says, many artists "are trying to make sense of their internal world and a lot of internal personal experiences that they're trying to give expression and meaning to through their art." Solitude allows for the reflection and observation necessary for that creative process.
passages.zh: 其中一个原因是，这些人很可能会独自花费持续的时间钻研自己的技艺。此外，Feist 说，许多艺术家“试图理解自己的内心世界，以及许多他们想通过艺术赋予其表达和意义的内在个人体验”。独处为这一创造过程所必需的反思和观察提供了条件。

passages.en: I) A recent justification of these ideas came from University at Buffalo psychologist Julie Bowker, who researches social withdrawal. Social withdrawal is usually categorised into three types: shyness caused by fear or anxiety; avoidance, from a dislike of socialising; and unsociability, from a preference for solitude. A paper by Bowker and her colleagues was the first to show that a type of social withdrawal could have a positive effect—they found that creativity was linked specifically to unsociability. They also found that unsociability had no correlation with aggression (shyness and avoidance did). This was significant because while previous research had suggested that unsociability might be harmless, Bowker and colleagues' paper showed that it could actually be beneficial. Unsociable people are likely to be "having just enough interaction," Bowker says. "They have a preference for being alone, but they also don't mind being with others."
passages.zh: 最近，布法罗大学研究社会退缩的心理学家 Julie Bowker 为这些观点提供了进一步的依据。社会退缩通常分为三种类型：由恐惧或焦虑引起的害羞；源于不喜欢社交的回避；以及源于偏好独处的不合群。Bowker 和她的同事发表的一篇论文首次表明，某种类型的社会退缩可能产生积极影响——他们发现，创造力与不合群之间存在特定联系。他们还发现，不合群与攻击性之间没有相关性（害羞和回避则与攻击性相关）。这一点意义重大，因为此前的研究虽然表明不合群可能没有危害，但 Bowker 及其同事的论文显示，不合群实际上可能有益。Bowker 说，不合群的人很可能“拥有恰到好处的互动”。“他们偏好独处，但也不介意与他人相处。”

passages.en: J) Still, it turns out that solitude is important for more than creativity. It's commonly believed that leaders need to be sociable. But this depends, among other things, on the personalities of their employees. One 2011 study showed that in branches of a pizza chain where employees were more passive, outgoing bosses were associated with higher profits. But in branches where employees were more active, introverted(内向的) leaders were more effective. One reason for this is that introverted people are less likely to feel threatened by strong personalities and suggestions. They're also more likely to listen.
passages.zh: 不过，事实证明，独处的重要性并不只体现在创造力方面。人们通常认为领导者需要善于社交。但这取决于多种因素，其中包括员工的性格。2011 年的一项研究显示，在某连锁披萨店员工较为被动的分店里，外向的老板往往与更高的利润相关；但在员工更加积极主动的分店里，内向的领导者则更为有效。其中一个原因是，内向的人不太容易受到强势性格和意见的威胁。他们也更有可能倾听。

passages.en: K) Since ancient times, meanwhile, people have been aware of a link between isolation and mental focus. After all, cultures with traditions of religious hermits(隐士) believe that solitude is important for enlightenment. Recent research has given us a better understanding of why. One benefit of unsociability is the brain's state of active mental rest, which goes hand-in-hand with the stillness of being alone. When another person is present, your brain can't help but pay some attention. This can be a positive distraction. But it's still a distraction.
passages.zh: 与此同时，自古以来，人们就意识到孤立与精神专注之间存在联系。毕竟，拥有宗教隐士传统的文化都相信，独处对于获得启蒙十分重要。近期研究让我们更好地理解了其中的原因。不合群的一个益处是，大脑会处于一种积极的心理休息状态，而这种状态与独处时的静谧相伴而生。当另一个人在场时，你的大脑会不由自主地分出一部分注意力。这可能是一种积极的干扰，但它终究还是一种干扰。

passages.en: L) Daydreaming in the absence of such distractions activates the brain's default-mode network. Among other functions, this network helps to consolidate memory and understand others' emotions. Giving free rein to a wandering mind not only helps with focus in the long term but strengthens your sense of both yourself and others. Paradoxically, therefore, periods of solitude actually help when it comes time to socialise once more. And the occasional absence of focus ultimately helps concentration in the long run.
passages.zh: 在没有这类干扰的情况下做白日梦，会激活大脑的默认模式网络。除其他功能外，该网络还有助于巩固记忆和理解他人的情绪。任由思绪漫游不仅有助于从长远来看保持专注，还能增强你对自己和他人的认识。因此，矛盾的是，一段段独处时光实际上会在我们再次进行社交时发挥作用。而偶尔缺乏专注，最终也会从长远来看帮助我们集中注意力。

passages.en: M) A more recent advocate of thoughtful and productive solitude is Susan Cain, author of *Quiet: The Power of Introverts in a World That Can't Stop Talking* and founder of Quiet Revolution, a company that promotes quiet and introvert-friendly workplaces. "These days, we tend to believe that creativity emerges from a decidedly unreserved socialising process, but in fact it requires sustained attention and deep focus," she says. "Also, humans are such absorbent social beings that when we surround ourselves with others, we automatically take in their opinions and aesthetics. To truly chart our own path or vision, we have to be willing to isolate ourselves, at least for some period of time."
passages.zh: Susan Cain 是较近期倡导富有思考且富有成效的独处的人。她是《安静：内向性格的竞争力》和 Quiet Revolution 的作者，也是 Quiet Revolution 的创始人。Quiet Revolution 是一家致力于推广安静且适合内向者的工作场所的公司。她说：“如今，我们往往认为创造力产生于一种明显不加节制的社交过程中，但事实上，创造力需要持续的注意力和深度的专注。此外，人类是如此容易受到社会影响的生物，以至于当我们与他人相处时，会自动吸收他们的观点和审美。要真正规划出属于自己的道路或愿景，我们必须愿意让自己与他人隔离，至少在一段时间内如此。”

passages.en: N) Still, the line between useful solitude and dangerous isolation can be blurry. "Almost anything can be adaptive and maladaptive, depending on how extreme they get," Feist says. A disorder has to do with dysfunction. If someone stops caring about people and cuts off all contact, this could point to an irrational neglect of social relations. But creative unsociability is a far cry from this. In fact, Feist says, "there's a real danger with people who are never alone." It's hard to examine one's own thoughts, feelings and motives, to be self-aware, and fully relaxed unless you have occasional solitude. In addition, introverts tend to have fewer but stronger friendships—which has been linked to greater happiness.
passages.zh: 不过，有益的独处与危险的孤立之间的界线可能很模糊。Feist 说：“几乎任何事情都可能具有适应性，也可能具有不适应性，这取决于其程度有多极端。”障碍与功能失调有关。如果一个人不再关心他人，并切断所有联系，这可能表明他在非理性地忽视社会关系。但富有创造力的不合群与此相去甚远。事实上，Feist 说：“从不独处的人确实面临着真正的危险。”除非偶尔独处，否则人很难审视自己的思想、感受和动机，形成自我意识，并得到充分放松。此外，内向者往往拥有较少但更牢固的友谊，而这与更高的幸福感有关。

passages.en: O) As with many things, quality reigns over quantity. Nurturing a few solid relationships without feeling the need to constantly populate your life with endless chatting ultimately may be better for you.
passages.zh: 和许多事情一样，质量胜过数量。用心维系几段牢固的关系，而不必觉得自己需要通过无休止的闲聊不断让生活充满他人，最终可能对你更有益。

passages.en: P) Thus, if your personality tends toward unsociability, you shouldn't feel the need to change. Of course, that comes with qualifications. But as long as you have regular social contact, you are choosing solitude rather than being forced into it, you have at least a few good friends and your solitude is good for your well-being or productivity, there's no point agonising over how to fit a square personality into a round hole.
passages.zh: 因此，如果你的性格倾向于不合群，就不必觉得自己需要改变。当然，这一结论也有一些条件。但只要你保持定期的社会交往，选择独处而不是被迫孤立，至少拥有几位好朋友，并且独处有益于你的身心健康或工作效率，就没有必要为如何把方形的性格塞进圆形的孔洞而苦恼。

statements.en: Lots of research demonstrates that being socially isolated is harmful to the elderly.
statements.zh: 大量研究表明,社交孤立对老年人有害。

analysis.锚点: 老年人 + 社交隔离有害
analysis.定位: C 段 Abundant research shows the harms of social isolation, considered a serious public health problem in countries that have rapidly ageing populations (though talk of a 'loneliness epidemic' may be exaggerated). 大量研究显示社交隔离的危害，它被视为快速老龄化国家的一项严重公共卫生问题（尽管「孤独流行病」的说法可能夸大其词）。
analysis.改写: Lots of research demonstrates↔Abundant research shows 同义词替换 being socially isolated is harmful↔the harms of social isolation 形容词结构 → 名词化 the elderly↔rapidly ageing populations 概括上位换写
analysis.辨邻: D D 段虽然也谈隔离的害处，但范围被锁在「极端且非自愿」的案例：被囚禁者、孤儿院儿童、单独监禁的犯人，Examples of people kept in captivity, children kept isolated in abusive orphanages, and prisoners kept in solitary confinement，并不针对「老年人 the elderly」这一人群，故不是 36 题的源头段。 prolonged solitude can lead to hallucinations(幻觉) and other forms of mental instability

statements.en: Being alone enables artists to think and observe, which is a must for their creation.
statements.zh: 独处使艺术家能够思考和观察,这是他们创作的必要条件。

analysis.锚点: 艺术家创作所需的思考与观察
analysis.定位: H 段 Solitude allows for the reflection and observation necessary for that creative process. 独处为这一创作过程所必需的反思与观察提供了空间。
analysis.改写: think and observe↔reflection and observation 动词 → 名词化 a must for their creation↔necessary for that creative process 口语化与正式表达互换 Being alone enables artists↔Solitude allows for 近义词替换 + 主语让位
analysis.辨邻: G G 段是 Feist 的研究结论 Feist's research on both artists and scientists shows that one of the most prominent features of creative folks is their lesser interest in socialising，并未出现「思考、观察、创作过程所需」的机制陈述。 a lack of concern for social norms

statements.en: To one writer, being forced to play with others was a penalty while being kept alone in a room was quite a pleasure.
statements.zh: 对一位作家来说,被迫与他人玩耍是一种惩罚,而独自待在房间里则是一种享受。

analysis.锚点: 作家：被迫和别人玩＝惩罚，独处＝乐事
analysis.定位: B 段 When parents on TV shows punished their kids by ordering them to go to their rooms, I was confused. I loved my room. Being there behind a locked door was a treat. To me a punishment was being ordered to play games with my cousin Louis. 当电视剧里的父母用「回房间去」来惩罚孩子时，我感到困惑。我爱我的房间。锁着门待在里面是一种享受。对我来说，惩罚是被要求和表哥 Louis 一起玩游戏。
analysis.改写: To one writer↔author Anneli Rufus 上位概括 being forced to play with others was a penalty↔a punishment was being ordered to play games with my cousin Louis 近义词替换 being kept alone in a room was quite a pleasure↔Being there behind a locked door was a treat 近义词替换 + 同景概括
analysis.辨邻: A A 段的「我」是文章作者本人，I'm sometimes secretly pleased when social plans are called off 与题干的「作家受罚说」无关，未提「被迫与人玩＝惩罚」这一独家细节。 I can be a reluctant socialiser

statements.en: Recent research shows for the first time that there is a specific link between being creative and being unsociable.
statements.zh: 最新研究首次表明,创造力与不善社交之间存在特定联系。

analysis.锚点: 首次发现：创造力与不爱社交专门挂钩
analysis.定位: I 段 A paper by Bowker and her colleagues was the first to show that a type of social withdrawal could have a positive effect—they found that creativity was linked specifically to unsociability. Bowker 及同事的一篇论文首次表明，一类社交回避行为可以带来正面效应——他们发现，创造力专门与「不爱社交」相关联。
analysis.改写: Recent research shows for the first time↔A paper by Bowker and her colleagues was the first to show 副词「first」直接保留 a specific link between being creative and being unsociable↔creativity was linked specifically to unsociability 副词 specifically 与形容词 specific 互换 + 形名互换
analysis.辨邻: G G 段中 Feist's research on both artists and scientists shows 给的是较早的总体结论，并无「首次发现」与「专门挂钩」的表述，主语是 Feist 而非 Bowker。 one of the most prominent features of creative folks is their lesser interest in socialising

statements.en: We must be willing to stay alone at least for some time in order to plot our own course.
statements.zh: 我们必须愿意至少在一段时间内独处,以便规划自己的道路。

analysis.锚点: 为「走自己的路」而愿意独处
analysis.定位: M 段 To truly chart our own path or vision, we have to be willing to isolate ourselves, at least for some period of time. 要真正规划我们自己的道路或愿景，我们必须愿意把自己与他人隔离开来，至少一段时间。
analysis.改写: plot our own course↔chart our own path or vision 罕见同源隐喻短语 We must be willing to stay alone at least for some time↔we have to be willing to isolate ourselves, at least for some period of time 近义短语对换 + 时间表达保留
analysis.辨邻: F F 段只是泛论 Solitude is a time for reflection, for thinking about things more deeply，没有「plot our own course / chart our own path」的目的状语，不是 40 题的源头段。 there are benefits in learning to love your solitude

statements.en: According to new research, for people who prefer being alone, solitude can be beneficial to their work lives and emotional health.
statements.zh: 根据新研究,对于喜欢独处的人来说,孤独对他们的工作生活和情绪健康都有益处。

analysis.锚点: 偏好独处者：工作 + 情绪健康双受益
analysis.定位: E 段 For those of us who just prefer plenty of alone time, emerging research suggests some good news: there are upsides to being alone—for both our work lives and our emotional well-being. 对于我们这些只是更喜欢有大量独处时间的人来说，新近的研究带来一些好消息：独处对我们的工作生活和情绪健康都有正面意义。
analysis.改写: According to new research, for people who prefer being alone↔For those of us who just prefer plenty of alone time, emerging research suggests 近义词替换 + 限定词保留 solitude can be beneficial to their work lives and emotional health↔there are upsides to being alone—for both our work lives and our emotional well-being 形 / 名互换 + 复合名词保留
analysis.辨邻: F F 段以散文化笔调说 Solitude is a time for reflection、something to be treasured，但既无 emerging / new research 这一研究信号，也没把「work lives + emotional well-being」并列起来。 there are benefits in learning to love your solitude

statements.en: It may turn out to be better for one to cultivate a few steady relationships than to busy themselves socialising.
statements.zh: 对一个人来说,培养几段稳定的关系可能比忙于社交更好。

analysis.锚点: 少数稳固关系 ＞ 忙于社交
analysis.定位: O 段 As with many things, quality reigns over quantity. Nurturing a few solid relationships without feeling the need to constantly populate your life with endless chatting ultimately may be better for you. 如同许多事一样，质量胜过数量。培育少数几段稳固的关系，而不必感到必须用无休止的闲聊把生活填满，从长远看也许对你更好。
analysis.改写: to cultivate a few steady relationships↔Nurturing a few solid relationships 近义动词 + 近义形容词 than to busy themselves socialising↔without feeling the need to constantly populate your life with endless chatting 比较结构同义改写 It may turn out to be better for one↔ultimately may be better for you 情态词与「最终」副词保留
analysis.辨邻: N N 段说 introverts tend to have fewer but stronger friendships—which has been linked to greater happiness，与本题相近但不带「质胜于量 quality reigns over quantity」与「不停闲聊」这两个题干精确锚点。 introverts tend to have fewer but stronger friendships

statements.en: Allowing your mind to wander freely is conducive to sharpening your focus in the long run.
statements.zh: 让思绪自由漫游从长远来看有助于提高专注力。

analysis.锚点: 放任思绪游走 → 长远更专注
analysis.定位: L 段 Giving free rein to a wandering mind not only helps with focus in the long term but strengthens your sense of both yourself and others. 放任游走的思绪不仅有助于长期保持专注，还会增强你对自我和他人的感知。
analysis.改写: Allowing your mind to wander freely↔Giving free rein to a wandering mind 近义习语 + 形名互换 is conducive to sharpening your focus in the long run↔helps with focus in the long term 近义动词 + 时间副词同义
analysis.辨邻: K K 段说 the brain's state of active mental rest, which goes hand-in-hand with the stillness of being alone，但「mind to wander freely」「focus in the long run」这两个题干关键锚点都在 L 段才出现。 When another person is present, your brain can't help but pay some attention

statements.en: Research conducted on artists and scientists indicates that creative people are less interested in hanging out with others.
statements.zh: 对艺术家和科学家进行的研究表明,有创造力的人对与他人交往不太感兴趣。

analysis.锚点: 对艺术家与科学家做的研究
analysis.定位: G 段 In fact, Feist's research on both artists and scientists shows that one of the most prominent features of creative folks is their lesser interest in socialising. 事实上，Feist 对艺术家与科学家的研究都表明，富有创造力的人最显著的特征之一是对社交的兴趣较低。
analysis.改写: Research conducted on artists and scientists↔Feist's research on both artists and scientists 近义动词 + 研究对象逐字复现 creative people are less interested in hanging out with others↔one of the most prominent features of creative folks is their lesser interest in socialising 口语 ↔ 正式词替换 + 比较级保留
analysis.辨邻: I I 段是 University at Buffalo psychologist Julie Bowker 的研究，谈的是社交回避的三种类型，并未明确说研究对象是 artists and scientists。 they found that creativity was linked specifically to unsociability

statements.en: According to Feist, you will have difficulty knowing yourself if you do not stay alone occasionally.
statements.zh: 根据Feist的观点,如果不偶尔独处,你将很难了解自己。

analysis.定位: N 段 It's hard to examine one's own thoughts, feelings and motives, to be self-aware, and fully relaxed unless you have occasional solitude. 除非你偶尔独处，否则很难审视自己的想法、感受与动机，做到自我觉察并彻底放松。
analysis.改写: According to Feist↔Feist says 信源逐字一致 you will have difficulty knowing yourself↔It's hard to examine one's own thoughts, feelings and motives, to be self-aware 概括上位 if you do not stay alone occasionally↔unless you have occasional solitude 否定句式等价
analysis.辨邻: G G 段中 Feist 的研究指向 lesser interest in socialising，并未提到「不独处便难自知」这一论断，故不是 45 题的源头段。 Gregory Feist, who focuses on the psychology of creativity

reading1.title: 2025年6月·第3套 英语六级阅读理解（四选一） 第 1 篇 · 46–50 题答案与解析

passages.en: Simulators are most often utilized within industries such as nuclear power, aviation and surgery where failure results in disastrous consequences. To maximize the value from a simulation learning experience, participants should immediately and directly apply their learning to a specific intervention within their organization.
passages.zh: 模拟器最常用于核电、航空和外科手术等行业，因为在这些行业中，失败会导致灾难性后果。为了最大限度地发挥模拟学习体验的价值，参与者应立即将所学内容直接应用于其组织中的一项具体干预措施。

passages.en: Most organizations aspire to deploy significant change programs, only to find them nearly impossible to implement. That is largely because successful change requires more than a vision, it requires a workforce that not only doesn't resist change, but embraces it.
passages.zh: 大多数组织都希望实施重大的变革计划，却发现这些计划几乎无法落实。这主要是因为成功的变革需要的不仅仅是愿景，还需要一支不仅不抵制变革、反而拥抱变革的员工队伍。

passages.en: To achieve success, an organization must build a transformation program that will allow change to be rapidly pulled across its departments and throughout its layers. Regardless of the level of senior management commitment, unless key thought leaders at all levels embrace the change, the initiative will wither and die. To create this kind of widespread passion, learning leaders must expose the workforce to what could be, which will enable them to rethink their mental models, enable them to break free from their deep-rooted paradigms and embrace the opportunity to learn.
passages.zh: 要取得成功，组织必须建立一项转型计划，使变革能够迅速在各部门之间及组织的各个层级中推进。无论高级管理层的支持程度如何，除非各个层级的关键思想领袖都接受变革，否则这一倡议终将衰败并消亡。为了激发这种广泛的热情，学习负责人必须让员工接触可能实现的情形，从而使他们能够重新思考自己的思维模式，摆脱根深蒂固的范式，并拥抱学习的机会。

passages.en: Allowing participants to enter a simulated environment provides them with the opportunity to experience alternative realities which can prompt them to rethink their current beliefs.
passages.zh: 允许参与者进入模拟环境，可以为他们提供体验其他现实的机会，从而促使他们重新思考当前的信念。

passages.en: Behavioral change is not easy for most adults. Lectures, training programs and workshops can explain the intellectual elements of transformation, but they are seldom effective at getting to the behavioral aspects that lie at the heart of a significant change initiative. Further, under normal working conditions, managers rarely see the full effect of their employee development efforts. As such, an intervention like a simulation can provide the stimulus for change.
passages.zh: 对大多数成年人来说，行为改变并不容易。讲座、培训项目和研讨会可以解释转型的理性要素，但它们很少能有效触及重大变革倡议核心的行为层面。此外，在正常的工作条件下，管理者很少能看到员工发展努力所产生的全部效果。因此，像模拟这样的干预措施可以为变革提供推动力。

passages.en: An effective simulation can be better than experience as a learning tool because it accelerates time, compresses space, and unlike reality, is specifically designed to maximize participant learning. Simulations provide an immersive learning experience where skills, processes and knowledge all can be highlighted in a way reality cannot. The ability to explore, experiment and repeatedly apply new knowledge in unlimited, risk-free models is what makes simulation one of the most productive forms of learning.
passages.zh: 作为一种学习工具，有效的模拟可能比实际经验更好，因为它能够加速时间、压缩空间，而且不同于现实，它是专门设计来最大限度地促进参与者学习的。模拟提供了一种沉浸式学习体验，使技能、流程和知识都能够以现实无法实现的方式得到突出呈现。在无限的、无风险的模型中探索、试验并反复应用新知识的能力，正是模拟成为最具成效的学习形式之一的原因。

passages.en: Well-designed simulations can enable individuals and groups to develop a deep level of understanding about how their decisions and intuitive responses to business stimuli affect their fellow participants and the organization as a whole. To reap the benefits, however, simulations must feel like reality. At the end of the successful simulation, participants must declare "this is us." If they don't, they will view the experience as a game, which can be difficult to apply on the job, or worse, irrelevant to everyday work tasks. To maximize benefits from simulation, participants should immediately apply the learning from the experience to forge a smooth link between learning and doing.
passages.zh: 设计良好的模拟能够使个人和群体深入理解：他们针对业务刺激所作出的决策和直觉反应，如何影响其他参与者以及整个组织。然而，要获得这些益处，模拟必须让人感觉像现实一样。成功的模拟结束时，参与者必须说：“这就是我们。”如果做不到这一点，他们就会把这种体验视为游戏，而这可能很难应用到工作中，或者更糟糕的是，认为它与日常工作任务无关。为了最大限度地发挥模拟的益处，参与者应立即将体验中学到的内容付诸实践，在学习与行动之间建立顺畅的联系。

questions.stem: What do we learn about successful changes in organizations?
questions.stem_zh: 关于组织中的成功变革,我们了解到什么?

options.text: They can be immediately implemented with great ease.
options.zh: 它们可以非常容易地立即实施。

options.text: They are usually led by organization leaders of vision.
options.zh: 它们通常由有远见的组织领导者引领。

options.text: They call for enthusiastic support from the workforce.
options.zh: 它们需要员工队伍的热情支持。

options.text: They often result from simulation learning experiences.
options.zh: 它们往往源于模拟学习体验。

questions.判型: 题干 What do we learn about successful changes in organizations? 是对客观信息的直接询问，没有 infer/imply 等推断信号，也没有 main idea/title 等主旨信号，属于典型细节题。
questions.拆句: What do we learn about successful changes in organizations? 是 What 引导的特殊疑问句，主干 we learn，about 介词短语限定 learn 的内容，successful changes 是真正的题眼，in organizations 是发生场域。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
questions.定位: P2 That is largely because successful change requires more than a vision, it requires a workforce that not only doesn't resist change, but embraces it. 这在很大程度上是因为成功的变革不只需要愿景，它还需要一支不但不抵触变革、还会拥抱变革的员工队伍。

locate.en: That is largely because successful change requires more than a vision, it requires a workforce that not only doesn't resist change, but embraces it.
locate.zh: 这在很大程度上是因为成功的变革不只需要愿景，它还需要一支不但不抵触变革、还会拥抱变革的员工队伍。

option_analysis.note: They can be immediately implemented with great ease. 称变革「轻易立刻落地」，但 Most organizations aspire to deploy significant change programs, only to find them nearly impossible to implement 明说大多数变革极难落地，两者完全相反。
They are usually led by organization leaders of vision. 把成功变革的关键归到「有远见的领导」上，但定位句 successful change requires more than a vision 恰恰说仅有 vision 不够，关键在 workforce；把强调点偷换了。
They call for enthusiastic support from the workforce. 的「require + 全员热情支持」与定位句 requires a workforce that ... embraces it 精准对位，且对位完整、无外加成分。

pairs.orig: it requires a workforce that not only doesn't resist change, but embraces it
pairs.opt: They call for enthusiastic support from the workforce.

option_analysis.note: They often result from simulation learning experiences. 说成功变革「源于」模拟学习，但全文逻辑是 simulation 服务于 change，并非 change 的来源；定位句也未涉及 simulation。

questions.stem: What should learning leaders do to arouse learners' passion for change?
questions.stem_zh: 学习领导者应该做什么来激发学习者对变革的热情?

options.text: Allow them to see what could possibly be achieved.
options.zh: 让他们看到可能实现的目标。

options.text: Help them break free from their old paradigms.
options.zh: 帮助他们摆脱旧有的范式。

options.text: Encourage them to rethink their thought models.
options.zh: 鼓励他们重新思考自己的思维模式。

options.text: Stimulate them to embrace fresh opportunities.
options.zh: 激励他们拥抱新的机会。

questions.判型: 题干 What should learning leaders do to arouse learners' passion for change? 在问主体的具体动作，答案对应原文里一句明确的「该做什么」，属细节题。
questions.拆句: What should learning leaders do to arouse learners' passion for change? 主干 What should learning leaders do，to arouse learners' passion for change 是目的状语，for change 进一步修饰 passion。结构清晰，无陷阱。
questions.定位: P3 To create this kind of widespread passion, learning leaders must expose the workforce to what could be, which will enable them to rethink their mental models, enable them to break free from their deep-rooted paradigms and embrace the opportunity to learn. 为了激发这种广泛的热情，learning leaders 必须把员工带去看「事情本可以是什么样」，这将使他们重新审视心智模型、挣脱根深蒂固的旧范式，并拥抱学习机会。

locate.en: To create this kind of widespread passion, learning leaders must expose the workforce to what could be, which will enable them to rethink their mental models, enable them to break free from their deep-rooted paradigms and embrace the opportunity to learn.
locate.zh: 为了激发这种广泛的热情，learning leaders 必须把员工带去看「事情本可以是什么样」，这将使他们重新审视心智模型、挣脱根深蒂固的旧范式，并拥抱学习机会。

option_analysis.note: 预判落在主句动作 expose…to what could be 上，A 用 allow them to see what could possibly be achieved 与之一一对应。

pairs.orig: expose the workforce to what could be
pairs.opt: Allow them to see what could possibly be achieved.

option_analysis.note: Help them break free from their old paradigms. 取自定位句后面的 which 从句中的并列动作 enable them to break free from their deep-rooted paradigms，那是 expose 之后的结果，而非 learning leaders 直接「应做」的动作。
Encourage them to rethink their thought models. 取自 which 从句中的 rethink their mental models，依然属于 expose 之后的结果，不是题干所问的直接动作。
Stimulate them to embrace fresh opportunities. 改写自 embrace the opportunity to learn，仍是 which 结果从句尾部的并列结果之一，不是题干问的 learning leaders 的直接动作。

questions.stem: What does the passage say about lectures, training programs and workshops?
questions.stem_zh: 文章关于讲座、培训项目和研讨会说了什么?

options.text: They are generally incapable of changing workers' behaviors on the job.
options.zh: 它们通常无法改变员工在工作中的行为。

options.text: They are interventions different from simulations in creating stimuli for change.
options.zh: 它们是不同于模拟的干预措施,用于创造变革的刺激。

options.text: They aim at transforming the behaviors of the workers in an organization.
options.zh: 它们旨在改变组织中员工的行为。

options.text: They help managers achieve the full effect of employee development efforts.
options.zh: 它们帮助管理者充分实现员工发展工作的效果。

questions.判型: What does the passage say about lectures, training programs and workshops? 是 say about + 主体的标准细节题问法，无推断信号。
questions.拆句: What does the passage say about lectures, training programs and workshops? 主干 What does the passage say，about 引出讨论对象，对象是三项并列名词。无从句、无否定，无陷阱。
questions.定位: P5 Lectures, training programs and workshops can explain the intellectual elements of transformation, but they are seldom effective at getting to the behavioral aspects that lie at the heart of a significant change initiative. 讲座、培训项目和工作坊能讲清变革的认知层面，但它们在触及行为层面（而行为层面恰是重大变革的核心）这件事上几乎无效。

locate.en: Lectures, training programs and workshops can explain the intellectual elements of transformation, but they are seldom effective at getting to the behavioral aspects that lie at the heart of a significant change initiative.
locate.zh: 讲座、培训项目和工作坊能讲清变革的认知层面，但它们在触及行为层面（而行为层面恰是重大变革的核心）这件事上几乎无效。

option_analysis.note: 预判「改不了行为」直接对应 generally incapable of changing workers' behaviors，两端的否定强度通过 seldom↔generally not 桥接成立。

pairs.orig: they are seldom effective at getting to the behavioral aspects
pairs.opt: They are generally incapable of changing workers' behaviors on the job.

pairs.orig: the behavioral aspects that lie at the heart of a significant change initiative

option_analysis.note: They are interventions different from simulations in creating stimuli for change. 把三者说成「在制造变革刺激上不同于 simulation 的干预」，原文只把它们与 simulation 在「能不能触及行为」上作对照，未把它们也定性为 intervention，更未谈它们「创造刺激」。
They aim at transforming the behaviors of the workers in an organization. 称它们「以改变行为为目标」，与原文「在行为层面 seldom effective」的判定方向相反——原文恰是说它们做不到这件事。

They help managers achieve the full effect of employee development efforts. 让三者「帮助管理者获得员工发展投入的全部成效」，但原文 managers rarely see the full effect of their employee development efforts 是说在常规工作里 managers 几乎看不到全部成效，且这一判断是关于「常规工作条件」整体，不是三者帮助下的状况。

questions.stem: What makes simulation one of the most fruitful forms of learning?
questions.stem_zh: 是什么使模拟成为最富有成效的学习形式之一?

options.text: Its capability of saving time by accelerating the immersive learning experience.
options.zh: 它能够通过加速沉浸式学习体验来节省时间。

options.text: Its potential for learners to examine their skills, knowledge and learning process.
options.zh: 它让学习者有可能审视自己的技能、知识和学习过程。

options.text: Its capability of providing all participants with a practical learning experience.
options.zh: 它能够为所有参与者提供实践性的学习体验。

options.text: Its potential for learners to explore, experiment and practice without any risk.
options.zh: 它让学习者有可能在没有任何风险的情况下探索、试验和实践。

questions.判型: What makes simulation one of the most fruitful forms of learning? 用「What makes X Y?」结构直问 simulation 之所以 fruitful 的原因，原文给出明确归因。
questions.拆句: What makes simulation one of the most fruitful forms of learning? make 引导 sb./sth. + 宾补结构，simulation 是宾语，one of the most fruitful forms of learning 是宾补；fruitful 与原文 productive 同义。无陷阱。
questions.定位: P6 The ability to explore, experiment and repeatedly apply new knowledge in unlimited, risk-free models is what makes simulation one of the most productive forms of learning. 在数量无限、零风险的模型里探索、实验并反复运用新知的能力，正是让 simulation 成为最高效学习方式之一的原因。

locate.en: The ability to explore, experiment and repeatedly apply new knowledge in unlimited, risk-free models is what makes simulation one of the most productive forms of learning.
locate.zh: 在数量无限、零风险的模型里探索、实验并反复运用新知的能力，正是让 simulation 成为最高效学习方式之一的原因。

option_analysis.note: Its capability of saving time by accelerating the immersive learning experience. 把 accelerates time 拎出来当主因，但原文里它只是 simulation 优点的描述之一，不是 is what makes 强调结构所归的原因。

Its potential for learners to examine their skills, knowledge and learning process. 取自 skills, processes and knowledge all can be highlighted，但原文是 processes（业务流程/作业过程），选项改成了 learning process（学习过程），主体偷换；且原文是 simulation 来 highlight，不是 learners 来 examine。

Its capability of providing all participants with a practical learning experience. 用 practical learning experience 模糊概括 simulation，未含 risk-free、reflect、experiment 等核心元素；原文 is what makes 主语处也并未用 practical 来归因。
D 保留了原文的三动词并列与 risk-free 条件，是唯一同时满足两项核心的选项。

pairs.orig: The ability to explore, experiment and repeatedly apply new knowledge
pairs.opt: Its potential for learners to explore, experiment and practice without any risk.

questions.stem: What should participants do in a simulation to reap the greatest benefits possible?
questions.stem_zh: 参与者在模拟中应该做什么才能获得最大可能的收益?

options.text: Take the experience as a mere game.
options.zh: 将这种体验仅仅当作游戏。

options.text: Apply promptly what they learn to their jobs.
options.zh: 将所学内容迅速应用到工作中。

options.text: Develop a deep level of understanding.
options.zh: 培养深层次的理解。

options.text: Strive to connect closely with their leaders.
options.zh: 努力与领导者建立紧密联系。

questions.判型: What should participants do in a simulation to reap the greatest benefits possible? 是问明确做法的标准细节题。
questions.拆句: What should participants do in a simulation to reap the greatest benefits possible? 主干 What should participants do，in a simulation 是地点状语，to reap the greatest benefits possible 是目的不定式，possible 后置修饰 benefits。无陷阱。
questions.定位: P7 To maximize benefits from simulation, participants should immediately apply the learning from the experience to forge a smooth link between learning and doing. 为最大化从模拟中获得的收益，参与者应立刻把从体验中所学应用到工作中，以打通「学」与「做」之间的桥梁。

locate.en: To maximize benefits from simulation, participants should immediately apply the learning from the experience to forge a smooth link between learning and doing.
locate.zh: 为最大化从模拟中获得的收益，参与者应立刻把从体验中所学应用到工作中，以打通「学」与「做」之间的桥梁。

option_analysis.note: Take the experience as a mere game. 让参与者「把体验当作单纯的游戏」，但 If they don't, they will view the experience as a game, which can be difficult to apply on the job 明确把「视为游戏」当作负面后果。
B 在副词（promptly ↔ immediately）、核心动作（apply what they learn ↔ apply the learning）与落点（to their jobs ↔ between learning and doing）三处与定位句完全对位。

pairs.orig: participants should immediately apply the learning from the experience
pairs.opt: Apply promptly what they learn to their jobs.

pairs.orig: to forge a smooth link between learning and doing

option_analysis.note: Develop a deep level of understanding. 取自 enable individuals and groups to develop a deep level of understanding，那是 simulation 的功效（果），不是参与者「应当做什么以最大化收益」（因）。
Strive to connect closely with their leaders. 让参与者「努力与领导紧密联系」，但全文从未要求 participants 去与 leaders 建立紧密联系，原文 forge a link 的对象是 learning 与 doing，不是 participants 与 leaders。

reading2.title: 2025年6月·第3套 英语六级阅读理解（四选一） 第 2 篇 · 51–55 题答案与解析

passages.en: GDP growth is not a good indicator of how well a country is performing, and should not be the primary goal of governments. Unlimited growth is not sustainable, and economic thinking is moving toward the idea that we should aim for sustainability in our economic models. But while a sustainable economy is vital to our future, it is a means to an end, not an end in itself.
passages.zh: 国内生产总值的增长并不是衡量一个国家发展状况的良好指标，也不应成为政府的首要目标。无限制的增长是不可持续的，经济学思想正在转向这样一种理念：我们的经济模式应当以可持续性为目标。然而，尽管可持续的经济对我们的未来至关重要，它只是实现目标的手段，而不是目标本身。

passages.en: The idea that governments should focus on happiness has its critics. There are concerns about how happiness can be measured. Is happiness not a fleeting and subjective psychological state? Don't different people experience different levels of happiness? Even on the broadest interpretation of 'happiness' as prosperity or 'life satisfaction', people want different things.
passages.zh: 政府应当把重点放在幸福上这一观点也有批评者。人们担心幸福难以衡量。幸福难道不是一种短暂且主观的心理状态吗？不同的人难道不会体验到不同程度的幸福吗？即使将“幸福”最宽泛地理解为繁荣或“生活满意度”，人们想要的东西也各不相同。

passages.en: Of course, governments cannot impose life satisfaction on citizens. But our happiness relies on collaborative efforts as a society. A government's obligation lies in creating conditions that promote prosperity. And there is good reason to suppose that such conditions exist, are globally applicable, and are discoverable through research.
passages.zh: 当然，政府无法把生活满意度强加给公民。但我们的幸福依赖于整个社会的共同努力。政府的责任在于创造促进繁荣的条件。我们有充分理由认为，这样的条件确实存在，适用于全球，并且可以通过研究加以发现。

passages.en: In a recently published article, philosopher Julian Baggini suggests we should focus on 'real wealth' for citizens, which does not depend on GDP growth. Access is key: people do not need to own, but rather access things that enable them to live well. Technological advances and changes in social behavior enable us to make more efficient use of the assets that we already have. And focusing on access to the resources people need to live better lives could help reduce inequality.
passages.zh: 哲学家朱利安·巴吉尼在最近发表的一篇文章中提出，我们应当关注公民的“真正财富”，这种财富并不依赖于国内生产总值的增长。获取是关键：人们不必拥有各种东西，而只需能够获得那些使他们得以过上美好生活的东西。技术进步和社会行为的变化使我们能够更有效地利用已经拥有的资产。而且，关注人们改善生活所需资源的获取，或许有助于减少不平等。

passages.en: As far as it goes, this has much in common with proposals tabled by 'happiness' advocates. But it sets the bar far too low for what governments can and should be doing for their citizens.
passages.zh: 就其涉及的范围而言，这一观点与“幸福”倡导者提出的建议有许多共同之处。但对于政府能够而且应当为公民做些什么，它所设定的标准实在太低了。

passages.en: For example, it's not clear how a 'real wealth' economy would remedy the epidemic of mental ill-health that plagues our society. In Western countries, at least—poor mental health is more detrimental to wellbeing than poverty. Over and above a vastly improved provision of therapeutic mental healthcare, there are preventative measures for improving mental health that governments could and should adopt. The WHO recommends establishing institutions that facilitate community participation—educational programs and interventions that provide skills for promoting mental wellbeing. It says a lot, however, that the WHO feels the need to appeal to the economic benefits of improving mental health to persuade governments that the cost of taking proposed measures is justified. As long as the economy is their priority, governments need go no further than ensuring citizens' continued productivity.
passages.zh: 例如，目前尚不清楚“真正财富”经济将如何解决困扰我们社会的心理健康问题流行这一现象。至少在西方国家，心理健康状况不佳对福祉的损害大于贫困。除了大幅改善心理健康治疗服务的供给之外，政府还可以并且应当采取一些预防性措施来改善心理健康。世界卫生组织建议建立促进社区参与的机构，并开展能够提供促进心理福祉技能的教育项目和干预措施。然而，世界卫生组织认为有必要诉诸改善心理健康所带来的经济利益，以说服政府采取所建议措施的成本是合理的，这一事实本身就说明了很多问题。只要经济仍是政府的优先事项，政府就不必再进一步，只需确保公民持续保持生产力即可。

passages.en: To demand that governments set the 'happiness' of citizens as their highest priority is to demand that they view citizens as ends in themselves.
passages.zh: 要求政府把公民的“幸福”置于最高优先地位，就是要求政府把公民本身视为目的。

questions.stem: What does the passage say is the more recent thinking of economic growth?
questions.stem_zh: 文章指出，关于经济增长的最新思考是什么?

options.text: It should be made sustainable.
options.zh: 应当使其可持续。

options.text: It is vital to the future of humanity.
options.zh: 它对人类的未来至关重要。

options.text: It should be governments' chief concern.
options.zh: 应当成为政府的首要关注点。

options.text: It is an indicator of government performance.
options.zh: 它是政府绩效的指标。

questions.判型: What does the passage say is the more recent thinking of economic growth\? 问「文章说……是什么」，要的是原文给出的具体表述，不是要考生推断。
questions.拆句: 主干是 What does the passage say is the more recent thinking of economic growth\?，what 是 say 的宾语，is 引导的从句作 say 的真正宾语；不要把 is 误读成主句谓语。结构清晰、无陷阱。
questions.定位: P1 Unlimited growth is not sustainable, and economic thinking is moving toward the idea that we should aim for sustainability in our economic models. 无限增长不可持续，经济思潮正转向「我们应当在经济模型中以可持续为目标」这一理念。

locate.en: Unlimited growth is not sustainable, and economic thinking is moving toward the idea that we should aim for sustainability in our economic models.
locate.zh: 无限增长不可持续，经济思潮正转向「我们应当在经济模型中以可持续为目标」这一理念。

option_analysis.note: 预判「应追求可持续」与 It should be made sustainable 字面同向，无需推断，直接锁定。

pairs.orig: we should aim for sustainability in our economic models

option_analysis.note: 原文说「可持续经济」对未来重要 a sustainable economy is vital to our future，主语是「sustainable economy」，而非 It（指 economic growth）本身。
原文明确 GDP growth … should not be the primary goal of governments，作者主张增长不应是政府首要关切，It should be governments' chief concern 正好相反。
原文首句即否定 GDP growth is not a good indicator of how well a country is performing，It is an indicator of government performance 正是这个被否定的旧观点。

questions.stem: Why are some people opposed to the idea that governments should focus on happiness?
questions.stem_zh: 为什么有些人反对政府应当关注幸福的观点?

options.text: Governments cannot impose happiness on citizens.
options.zh: 政府无法将幸福强加给公民。

options.text: People's happiness is built upon their own endeavor.
options.zh: 人们的幸福建立在自己的努力之上。

options.text: Happiness means different things to different people.
options.zh: 幸福对不同的人意味着不同的事物。

options.text: Happiness depends on sustainable economic growth.
options.zh: 幸福依赖于可持续的经济增长。

questions.判型: Why are some people opposed to the idea that governments should focus on happiness\? 问「反对的原因」，原文必有一段集中陈述反对理由。
questions.拆句: 主干 Why are some people opposed to the idea，后接 that 引导的同位语从句解释 idea 的内容；opposed to 是固定搭配「反对」，不要看成被动语态。
questions.定位: P2 Even on the broadest interpretation of 'happiness' as prosperity or 'life satisfaction', people want different things. 即使把「幸福」理解到最宽泛的程度——视为「繁荣」或「生活满意度」——人们想要的东西也各不相同。

locate.en: Even on the broadest interpretation of 'happiness' as prosperity or 'life satisfaction', people want different things.
locate.zh: 即使把「幸福」理解到最宽泛的程度——视为「繁荣」或「生活满意度」——人们想要的东西也各不相同。

option_analysis.note: Governments cannot impose happiness on citizens 是作者本人的让步（governments cannot impose life satisfaction on citizens），而非反对者的反对原因，时空错位。
原文 P2 从未提到「幸福建立在个人努力上」；endeavor 在全文不存在，是凭空添加的因果。
「幸福因人而异」与 Happiness means different things to different people 同义，三个反问句的共同指向皆收束于此。

pairs.opt: Happiness means different things to different people

pairs.orig: Don't different people experience different levels of happiness\?
pairs.opt: Happiness means different things to different people

option_analysis.note: P1 把 sustainable 与 happiness 视为两条不同线索，原文从未说 Happiness depends on sustainable economic growth；该选项把两个概念强行嫁接。

questions.stem: What does philosopher Julian Baggini suggest governments do in a recently published article?
questions.stem_zh: 哲学家Julian Baggini在最近发表的一篇文章中建议政府做什么?

options.text: Try to reduce inequality between the rich and the poor.
options.zh: 努力减少贫富之间的不平等。

options.text: Provide people with access to resources for a better life.
options.zh: 为人们提供获得更好生活的资源渠道。

options.text: Change people's behaviors to put social wealth to better use.
options.zh: 改变人们的行为以更好地利用社会财富。

options.text: Make use of advanced technologies to improve people's lives.
options.zh: 利用先进技术改善人们的生活。

questions.判型: What does philosopher Julian Baggini suggest governments do 是经典「某人的具体主张」型细节题。
questions.拆句: 主干 What does philosopher Julian Baggini suggest governments do，suggest 后接省略 that 的宾语从句 governments do (what)，what 是 do 的宾语前置——理解为「Baggini 建议政府做什么」。
questions.定位: P4 Access is key: people do not need to own, but rather access things that enable them to live well. 「使用权」是关键：人们不必拥有，而是要能用上那些让他们生活得更好的东西。

locate.en: Access is key: people do not need to own, but rather access things that enable them to live well.
locate.zh: 「使用权」是关键：人们不必拥有，而是要能用上那些让他们生活得更好的东西。

option_analysis.note: could help reduce inequality 只是 Baggini 主张的「附带效益」（could help），不是其建议政府该做的核心；选项 A 把附带效益当成主张主体。
预判「让公民能用上让生活更好的资源」与 Provide people with access to resources for a better life 字面同向。

pairs.orig: access things that enable them to live well
pairs.opt: Provide people with access to resources for a better life

option_analysis.note: 原文说 changes in social behavior enable us to make more efficient use of the assets，是「社会行为已发生的变化」让现有资产用得更高效；选项把它改成「政府去改变人们行为以更好利用社会财富」，主动者与目的都被偷换。
Technological advances 在原文同样只是 access 模型成立的「条件」，不是 Baggini 给政府的建议；选项 D 抓了边缘条件而漏掉主张句。

questions.stem: Why does the WHO feel the need to appeal to the economic benefits of improving mental health to justify its recommendations?
questions.stem_zh: 为什么WHO认为有必要诉诸改善心理健康的经济效益来证明其建议的合理性?

options.text: Mental health programs cannot be executed without GDP growth.
options.zh: 没有GDP增长就无法执行心理健康项目。

options.text: Psychological interventions are conducive to people's wellbeing.
options.zh: 心理干预有助于人们的幸福感。

options.text: Poor mental health is detrimental to a nation's economic system.
options.zh: 心理健康不良对国家经济体系有害。

options.text: Governments still take economic development as their priority.
options.zh: 政府仍然将经济发展作为优先事项。

questions.判型: Why does the WHO feel the need to appeal to the economic benefits 问「WHO 为何觉得有必要诉诸经济利益」，答案不在 WHO 这句的字面，而要从作者紧接的评论中推断政府的倾向。
questions.拆句: 主干 Why does the WHO feel the need to appeal to the economic benefits of improving mental health to justify its recommendations\?，feel the need to do = 觉得有必要做，to justify 是目的状语——「为了让其建议显得合理」。
questions.定位: P6 It says a lot, however, that the WHO feels the need to appeal to the economic benefits of improving mental health to persuade governments that the cost of taking proposed measures is justified. As long as the economy is their priority, governments need go no further than ensuring citizens' continued productivity. 然而，WHO 不得不诉诸「改善心理健康带来的经济收益」来说服政府这一举措的成本合理，这一点本身就说明了问题：只要政府仍把经济置于首位，他们就只关心公民能否继续创造产值。

locate.en: It says a lot, however, that the WHO feels the need to appeal to the economic benefits of improving mental health to persuade governments that the cost of taking proposed measures is justified. As long as the economy is their priority, governments need go no further than ensuring citizens' continued productivity.
locate.zh: 然而，WHO 不得不诉诸「改善心理健康带来的经济收益」来说服政府这一举措的成本合理，这一点本身就说明了问题：只要政府仍把经济置于首位，他们就只关心公民能否继续创造产值。

option_analysis.note: 原文从未说「无 GDP 增长就执行不了心理健康项目」，仅说「政府要看到经济收益才肯掏钱」；选项 A 把动机改成了执行前提，凭空捏造。
Psychological interventions are conducive to people's wellbeing 是事实陈述，原文 improving mental health 也支持这一点，但题干问的是「WHO 为何要诉诸经济收益」，与「干预有益健康」无关。
原文强调「政府以经济为先」是导致 WHO 必须用经济话术的「原因」；选项 C 反过来说「心理健康差对经济不利」是 WHO 用经济话术的原因——把工具变成了动机来源。
「政府只听经济话术」的根本原因即「政府仍以经济为先」，与 Governments still take economic development as their priority 同义。

pairs.orig: As long as the economy is their priority
pairs.opt: Governments still take economic development as their priority

pairs.orig: It says a lot, however, that the WHO feels the need to appeal to the economic benefits
pairs.opt: Governments still take economic development as their priority

questions.stem: What message does the author try to convey at the end of the passage?
questions.stem_zh: 作者在文章结尾试图传达什么信息?

options.text: Governments' goal should be prosperity-driven.
options.zh: 政府的目标应当以繁荣为导向。

options.text: Governments' goal should be people-oriented.
options.zh: 政府的目标应当以人为本。

options.text: Governments should consider citizens' views in decision-making.
options.zh: 政府在决策时应当考虑公民的观点。

options.text: Governments should set sustained productivity as their top priority.
options.zh: 政府应当将持续生产力设为首要任务。

questions.判型: What message does the author try to convey at the end of the passage\? 问作者结尾要传达的核心信息，是局部主旨题。
questions.拆句: 主干 What message does the author try to convey at the end of the passage\?，try to convey = 试图传达；message 是宾语前置至 what。

option_analysis.note: 全文反对把繁荣/产值当目标（should not be the primary goal / ensuring citizens' continued productivity 被作者批评），Governments' goal should be prosperity-driven 正好是作者反对的立场。
末段「把公民视为目的」是全文落点，与 Governments' goal should be people-oriented 同义。

pairs.orig: view citizens as ends in themselves
set the 'happiness' of citizens as their highest priority

option_analysis.note: 原文从未谈及「决策时听取公民意见」（views in decision-making）；这是把「以人为本」误解为「问政于民」，添加了原文不存在的程序性内容。
作者在 governments need go no further than ensuring citizens' continued productivity 中明显嘲讽了「以产值为先」的政府逻辑；sustained productivity as their top priority 正是作者批评的对象。

translation.title: 2025年6月·第3套英语六级汉译英（段落翻译） · 客观介绍南水北调工程 参考译文与解析
translation.directions: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to translate a passage from Chinese into English. You should write your answer on Answer Sheet 2.
translation.source_zh: 自古以来,中国的水资源北缺南丰,分布极不均衡。为了有效解决北方严重缺水问题,中国政府实施了南水北调工程(the South-to-North Water Diversion Project)。这是一项跨区域配置水资源的宏大水利工程。历经数十年的规划与筹备,工程于2002年开工建设,分为东、中、西三条线路,总长4350公里,惠及人口将超过4亿。自2014年通水以来,工程向北方调水累计已超500亿立方米,为北方地区的人民提供了可靠的水资源,同时也极大地改善了这一地区的生态环境,促进了经济的可持续健康发展。
translation.reference_en:
Since ancient times, China's water resources have been unevenly distributed, with water scarce in the north but abundant in the south. To effectively address the severe water shortage in the north, the Chinese government launched the South-to-North Water Diversion Project. It is a massive cross-regional water conservancy project for allocating water resources. After decades of planning and preparation, the project began construction in 2002. Divided into eastern, central and western routes with a total length of 4,350 kilometers, it is expected to benefit more than 400 million people. Since the water supply began in 2014, the project has diverted over 50 billion cubic meters of water to the north, providing reliable water resources for people in the region, while greatly improving the local ecological environment and promoting sustainable and healthy economic development.
【衔接】
第3句承接第2句的工程第2句末出现工程全名，第3句 这是一项……宏大水利工程 的「这」直接用 It 承接，避免重复整个工程名，已在 finalSentence 用 It is... 处理，读起来自然。
第4、5句用 it 回指工程避免重复第4句下半与第5句主语都是「工程」，不必每句重写 the project，改用 it 承接（第4句后半 it is expected、第5句可用 the project 一次后续用 it），既显衔接又免重复，符合英文少重复名词的习惯。
第5句成果间补 while 显伴随第5句 同时也极大地改善了 的「同时也」点明后续成果与主成果是并行伴随关系，英文补 while + doing 把这层「在提供水的同时还带来……」的逻辑显化，比单纯 and 罗列更连贯。

cohesion.detail: 第2句末出现工程全名，第3句 这是一项……宏大水利工程 的「这」直接用 It 承接，避免重复整个工程名，已在 finalSentence 用 It is... 处理，读起来自然。

cohesion.core: 第4、5句用 it 回指工程避免重复
cohesion.detail: 第4句下半与第5句主语都是「工程」，不必每句重写 the project，改用 it 承接（第4句后半 it is expected、第5句可用 the project 一次后续用 it），既显衔接又免重复，符合英文少重复名词的习惯。

cohesion.core: 第5句成果间补 while 显伴随
cohesion.detail: 第5句 同时也极大地改善了 的「同时也」点明后续成果与主成果是并行伴随关系，英文补 while + doing 把这层「在提供水的同时还带来……」的逻辑显化，比单纯 and 罗列更连贯。

main_idea.core: 客观介绍南水北调工程
main_idea.detail: 全段是一篇典型的中国国情/重大工程介绍说明文，开篇 自古以来,中国的水资源北缺南丰,分布极不均衡 摆事实，随后客观陈述工程的目的、规模、线路与成效。语体是中性、客观的事实陈述，不带个人情感，这正是六级汉译英最常见的「中国文化/社会/经济介绍」题材。

tense.detail: 全篇主体是对工程现状与客观事实的陈述（它是什么工程、分几条线、惠及多少人），故主时态用一般现在时。但本篇内嵌明确的历史与时间节点：工程于2002年开工建设 是过去发生的动作，用一般过去时；自2014年通水以来,工程向北方调水累计已超500亿立方米 含「自……以来 + 累计」，是延续到现在的结果，用现在完成时。即「以现在时为锚，叙述具体动作时按时间节点偏离」。

term_notes.detail: 原文已直接给出官方英译 南水北调工程(the South-to-North Water Diversion Project)，括号里就是约定俗成的官方译名，照抄即可：the South-to-North Water Diversion Project。全篇再次提到时统一用 the project 承接，不得另造译法。
这是一项跨区域配置水资源的宏大水利工程 中「水利工程」是文化/专业负载词，统一译为 water conservancy project（或 water diversion project）；本篇因前句已点名工程，此处可直接用 a massive cross-regional water diversion project 承接，避免与专名重复。

steps.text: 水资源 + 分布 + 不均衡（主语策略：原句主语）中文主语是「水资源」，谓语核心是「分布……不均衡」。立骨架：China's water resources are unevenly distributed。中国的水资源……分布极不均衡 提为主干，「北缺南丰」作为分布不均衡的具体说明降级处理。

北缺南丰降级为分词/介词结构北缺南丰 是对「分布不均衡」的进一步说明，不要照中文用 and 平铺成 the north lacks and the south is rich。可降级成 with 独立结构作伴随状语：with the north short of water and the south abundant in it；自古以来 译为句首时间状语 Since ancient times。
时态回指全篇基调，陈述客观长期事实，用一般现在时 are distributed；「自古以来」只是强调由来已久，不必改成完成时。 单复数water resources 作「水资源」固定用复数；the north / the south 特指中国的南北方，加定冠词 the。
Since ancient times, China's water resources have been unevenly distributed, with water scarce in the north but abundant in the south.
中国政府 + 实施 + 工程（主语策略：原句主语）主语是 中国政府（the Chinese government），谓语「实施」译 launched / implemented，宾语是工程。骨架：The Chinese government launched the South-to-North Water Diversion Project。
为了……降级为不定式目的状语为了有效解决北方严重缺水问题 降级成 To effectively address the severe water shortage in the north 置于句首作目的状语；专名照抄括号里的官方译名。

时态「实施了」是已完成的具体动作，结合下文 2002 年开工的历史脉络，本句用一般过去时 launched，属对全篇现在时基调的合理偏离。 用词「解决问题」避免一律用 solve，address / tackle the problem 更地道；「严重缺水」译 severe water shortage。 专名工程名照抄原文括号官方译名 the South-to-North Water Diversion Project，首字母大写、不可自译。
To effectively address the severe water shortage in the north, the Chinese government launched the South-to-North Water Diversion Project.
这 + 是 + 宏大水利工程（主语策略：原句主语）典型的 A is B 判断句。主语「这」指代上句的工程，译 It；系动词 is；表语是「宏大水利工程」。骨架：It is a massive water conservancy project。

跨区域配置水资源作前后置定语跨区域配置水资源的 是修饰「工程」的长定语：「跨区域」用形容词 cross-regional 前置，「配置水资源」用现在分词短语 allocating water resources 后置。译为 a massive cross-regional water conservancy project for allocating water resources，长定语前后分流，不全堆在名词前。
时态回指全篇基调，下定义属客观事实，用一般现在时 is。 冠词首次引入这个工程作为一类事物来定义，用不定冠词 a：a massive project。
It is a massive cross-regional water conservancy project for allocating water resources.
工程 + 开工建设（主语策略：原句主语）这是一句多动词的长流水句，但核心主谓只有一个：主语 工程（the project），核心谓语是 于2002年开工建设（began construction in 2002）。其余「历经……」「分为……」「总长……」「惠及……」全是围绕工程的附加信息，须降级，不能全提成并列谓语。

四个附加信息分别降级安放历经数十年的规划与筹备→现在分词短语前置 After decades of planning and preparation；分为东、中、西三条线路→过去分词作定语 divided into eastern, central and western routes；总长4350公里→with 独立结构 with a total length of 4,350 kilometers；惠及人口将超过4亿→另起独立句或定语从句 and is expected to benefit more than 400 million people。四股信息各用不同从属结构挂上，避免 and 一路平铺。

时态「2002年开工」是过去明确时点，用一般过去时 began；「惠及人口将超过4亿」含「将」，是预期，用 is expected to benefit / will benefit，体现一般现在/将来。 语态「分为三条线路」是工程「被」分，用被动 be divided into/is divided into；本篇用过去分词 divided 作定语承接。 数字与单位4350 公里写 4,350 kilometers；4 亿写 400 million（不是 4 hundred million，hundred 不加 s）；线路是三条，routes 用复数。

After decades of planning and preparation, the project began construction in 2002. Divided into eastern, central and western routes with a total length of 4,350 kilometers, it is expected to benefit more than 400 million people.

工程 + 调水/提供/改善/促进（主语策略：原句主语）主语仍是 工程（the project，可用 it 承接）。这句有多个并列动作：「调水超500亿立方米」「提供水资源」「改善生态环境」「促进发展」。可让「调水」作主干谓语，后三个「提供/改善/促进」处理成并列谓语或分词结果状语。骨架：the project has diverted over 50 billion cubic meters of water。

自……以来前置 + 后续成果降级自2014年通水以来→Since the water supply began in 2014 作时间状语前置；为北方地区的人民提供了可靠的水资源 与主干并列；同时也极大地改善了这一地区的生态环境,促进了经济的可持续健康发展→用现在分词作结果状语 greatly improving the local ecological environment and promoting sustainable and healthy economic development，把后两项成果降级成伴随/结果，主次分明。

时态「自2014……以来……累计已超」是从过去延续到现在的累积结果，用现在完成时 has diverted；后续 provided/providing 与 improving 保持同一时间框架。这是本篇唯一最该用完成时之处，务必识别「自……以来 + 已/累计」这一信号。 主谓一致主语 the project 是第三人称单数，完成时助动词用 has（has diverted），不是 have。 数字与单位500 亿 = 50 billion；「立方米」cubic meters 用复数。

Since the water supply began in 2014, the project has diverted over 50 billion cubic meters of water to the north, providing reliable water resources for people in the region, while greatly improving the local ecological environment and promoting sustainable and healthy economic development.
